plain_summary: The EU(7)-PIM panel found no proven benefit and an unfavourable balance of benefit and harm for these vein medicines in older people. It reported that most vasodilators increase the risk of low blood pressure on standing and falls.

medicine_groups.name: Venotonic vein medicines
medicine_groups.note: Escin is also called aescin. None of these has a known Australian brand, so a history shows the ingredient name. Diosmin and compression stockings are not in this group. Count escin or aescin when listed as an active ingredient in its own right. Exclude horse chestnut extract when escin or aescin appears only as the substance used to standardise the extract. Include hidrosmin gel labelled for venous insufficiency. Exclude local bruise preparations.

rule_for_models: At age 65 or older, flag one systemic supply of hidrosmin, escin (aescin), vincamine with rutoside or troxerutin with vincamine, or a supply of hidrosmin gel labelled for venous insufficiency. Count escin or aescin only when listed as an active ingredient in its own right. Exclude local bruise preparations and horse chestnut extract that mentions escin or aescin only to describe its standardisation. If age, preparation or route is unclear and a supply could qualify, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm the missing information. A recorded age below 65 gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was started, whether the person has leg swelling or vein disease, whether compression stockings are used, and medicines bought over the counter or as complementary products.
ask_the_gp: Whether the vein medicine is still needed, and whether compression stockings or another approach could replace it.
